question: A marketing team wants to move its weekly performance report from the deepest-reasoning model to a lighter one to save allowance. What should they do first?
options: A) Ask Claude whether a lighter model could produce the same report to the same standard.
B) Switch the report over immediately, and change back if anyone complains about the quality.
C) Shorten the report first, so that a lighter model would have less material to work through each week.
D) Produce next week's report on both tiers and compare them against what the report must deliver.
correct_answers: D) Produce next week's report on both tiers and compare them against what the report must deliver.
explanations: Incorrect. That answer is a general claim about models rather than evidence from their own report.
Incorrect. Waiting for complaints makes readers the quality check, and subtle thinning of the analysis rarely produces a complaint.
Incorrect. Cutting scope changes the deliverable rather than testing whether the lighter tier can produce it.
Correct. A side-by-side run on their own work, judged against an agreed standard, is the only evidence that tells them whether the cheaper tier is adequate here.
